content.title: Layout Investigation: Find the Broken Relationship
content.hook: Good layout debugging is not “try CSS until it looks okay.”
content.context:
You are looking for the rule that controls the relationship you care about.

Use this loop:

**describe the intended relationship → inspect the parent → inspect the relevant layout property → make the smallest change → verify the changed case**
goals: Investigate a layout defect by identifying the intended relationship, observing the active rule, and making the smallest justified change.

activities.title: Interactive Flexbox & CSS Grid Layout Studio
activities.instruction: Manipulate flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, gap, and 2D CSS Grid tracks with live element reflow.

content.title: Interactive Flexbox & CSS Grid Layout Studio
content.description: Manipulate flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, gap, and 2D CSS Grid tracks with live element reflow.

interactive.caption: Manipulate flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, gap, and 2D CSS Grid tracks with live element reflow.

options.text: Whether `flex-direction` is creating the vertical arrangement.
Whether the button text is spelled correctly.
Whether the page needs a new HTML document.
Whether the screen is too bright.

feedback.correct: The symptom is directly connected to the direction rule. Start with the rule that controls the relationship instead of changing unrelated properties.
feedback.incorrect: Spelling, HTML document structure, and screen brightness do not stack flex items vertically. Inspect `flex-direction: column` on `.toolbar`, since that property directly controls the main axis.

options.text: `align-items`
`color`
`border-radius`
`font-size`

feedback.correct: The problem is cross-axis placement. `align-items` is the property that expresses that relationship for the flex container.
feedback.incorrect: Properties like `color`, `border-radius`, and `font-size` do not control vertical placement in a horizontal flex row. Inspect `align-items`, which controls cross-axis alignment.

content.question:
A three-column grid looks fine wide and cramped narrow.

You see no responsive rule.

What is the smallest useful question?

options.text: At what available width does this relationship stop working, and should the grid change there?
How can I add 40 random margins?
How can I hide the cards?
How can I delete half the content?

feedback.correct: The symptom is about the relationship between the grid and the available width. Find the constraint boundary before changing unrelated styles.
feedback.incorrect: Adding random margins or deleting content masks the issue. Ask at what available width the three-column relationship stops fitting and needs a responsive rule.

options.text: `flex-wrap: wrap`
`color: red`
`border: none`
`font-weight: bold`

feedback.correct: The intended relationship includes another row when space runs out. `flex-wrap: wrap` expresses that directly.
feedback.incorrect: Visual styles like `color`, `border`, or `font-weight` do not allow a single-line flex row to wrap. Add `flex-wrap: wrap` so items can flow onto a new line when space runs out.

activities.title: Smallest-fix challenge
activities.instruction: Inspect the broken `.toolbar` and `.cards` rules, apply the smallest justified CSS fixes to restore the intended relationships, and run the preview.

content.prompt:
The workspace below has two relationship bugs:
1. `.toolbar` should arrange its brand and status badge in a horizontal row (`flex-direction: row;`) vertically centered (`align-items: center;`), but it currently stacks them in a top-left column.
2. `.cards` should allow its 180px cards to wrap onto a new row when space runs out (`flex-wrap: wrap;`), but they currently stay on a single overflowing line.

Make only the targeted relationship fixes in `.toolbar` and `.cards`, then run the preview to verify the repaired layout.
content.htmlFixture:
Forge Inspector
Toolbar Aligned
Card A (180px)
Card B (180px)
Card C (180px)

testCases.description: Restores horizontal main axis on `.toolbar` with `flex-direction: row;`
Centers `.toolbar` items on the cross axis with `align-items: center;`
Allows `.cards` items to wrap onto additional lines with `flex-wrap: wrap;`

feedback.correct: Your CSS updates only the three controlling relationship properties: `flex-direction: row;`, `align-items: center;`, and `flex-wrap: wrap;`. In the preview, the toolbar now aligns horizontally and the 180px cards wrap cleanly instead of overflowing.
feedback.incorrect: Trace each symptom to its controlling rule: set `flex-direction: row;` and `align-items: center;` on `.toolbar`, and add `flex-wrap: wrap;` on `.cards`.

content.question: Which investigation order is most reliable?

options.text: Intended relationship → controlling rule → smallest change → verify.
Random changes → refresh → random changes.
Rewrite the whole page → inspect later.
Change every spacing value first.

feedback.correct: Good layout investigation starts with a model of the intended relationship and changes only the rule you have reason to suspect.
feedback.incorrect: Changing random spacing values or rewriting the whole page makes it harder to tell what fixed or broke the layout. Start from the intended relationship, identify the controlling rule, and test the smallest change.

activities.title: Diagnose & Fix: Broken Navigation Header
activities.instruction: Inspect the broken header in `Yours` or `Compare` view, identify the three broken layout relationships, and apply the smallest CSS fix.

content.prompt: The `.studio-nav` header is accidentally stacked vertically (`flex-direction: column`), pushed to the start instead of spaced apart, and `.nav-links` has `gap: 0px;` so the links collide. Fix `.studio-nav` (`flex-direction: row; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center;`) and `.nav-links` (`gap: 16px;`).
hints: On `.studio-nav`, change `flex-direction: column;` to `flex-direction: row;`, `justify-content: flex-start;` to `justify-content: space-between;`, and `align-items: flex-start;` to `align-items: center;`.
On `.nav-links`, change `gap: 0px;` to `gap: 16px;` so the three links have breathing room.

styleRules.description: Restores horizontal main axis (flex-direction: row) on .studio-nav
Distributes brand and links with justify-content: space-between on .studio-nav

feedback.correct: All four broken layout relationships are repaired: `.studio-nav` is back on a horizontal row with `space-between` and `center` alignment, and `.nav-links` separates its items with `gap: 16px`.
feedback.incorrect: Some broken layout rules remain — check `.studio-nav` (`flex-direction: row`, `justify-content: space-between`, `align-items: center`) and `.nav-links` (`gap: 16px`).

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Layout bugs are relationship bugs.
**Senior habit:** Make the smallest change that tests your hypothesis.
**Mastery signal:** You can identify the controlling layout property from a visible symptom before editing anything.
